score_change_reason: I raised the score by 1 because the reported 255-month evidence (mean |corr| 0.194, median 0.168, channel preservation 0.895) materially weakens the strict near-duplicate thesis versus H_1674. I still hold a reject-until-validated stance due crisis-regime orthogonality breakdown risk, missing Gate-15/TDC pass evidence, and incomplete PIT/timing implementation proof.

agreements.point: I agree that regime-conditional tail dependence is the key hidden failure mode: low average correlation is insufficient when p95 |corr| is ~0.447 and CRISIS TDC can spike exactly when diversification is needed.
I agree that 2020-2026 orthogonality deterioration (mean |corr| 0.2437 with multiple >0.5 months) directly supports my concern that diversifier behavior is regime-dependent and can fail in stress.

rebuttals.point: I disagree with the implied readiness at 15/20. Core controls are still unproven in artifacts (INV13 registry, lookahead suite, C11 timing, crisis TDC), so admission should remain blocked until evidence is passed, not just conditionally planned.

I disagree that shift(1L) effectively settles PIT risk. It addresses one leakage path, but timestamp-level publication availability and execution-clock alignment across all stack inputs are still not formally demonstrated.

I disagree with the claim that ICIR gate passage is 'certain.' The estimate is pre-cost and assumes stable correlation dynamics; turnover stress and crisis misclassification can still push realized ICIR below threshold.

strongest_opposing_argument: The strongest challenge to my original position is the empirical non-equivalence case: across 255 months, v2 materially reduces dependence on H_1674 (mean |corr| 0.194) while preserving foreign-flow information (0.895), indicating it is more than parameter reweighting.
kill_scenarios_update: New kill scenarios: (1) expanding beta_t quasi-constantization causes slow adaptation after structural breaks (foreign exodus/retail surge), (2) 21d lookback likely causes turnover hard-fail (>600%) and cost-driven alpha collapse, (3) crisis-regime tail cohabitation with H_1674/STR_1631 despite low mean correlation.
